newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Supported but trading interest thin.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Supported but trading interest thin.

text.p: Talk in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was thin on Monday but prices were well supported and firm sentiment was likely to continue amid tighter summer supplies, traders said.
The 180-cst grade was offered at $104.50 per tonne for mid-June delivery by a major while a bid was seen at $103.50 for late-June, traders said.
A total of four cargoes exchanged hands last week, with the first cargo at $101.00 per tonne and the rest at $103.00, mainly among majors.
"It was routine trade among majors last week without much of a surprise," said one trader.
A 20,000-tonne cargo of 380-cst bunker spec was offered at $96.00 per tonne on Monday for early June but there was no buying interest.
Bunker suppliers said firm cargo levels had forced them to raise offers but shipowners stayed on the sidelines, unwilling to pay high prices or turning to other ports with lower offers.
There had been some speculation that a local trader might emerge to bid up the market before the summer season, when fewer cargoes would come to Asia from the Middle East.
"It seems it's focus is still largely on the gas oil market but not on the fuel oil market," said another trader.
On the demand side, Taiwan's state Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) will close its import tender for one or two cargoes of 0.5-percent fuel oil for July delivery on May 21.
The tender will be valid for two days.
In the LSWR market, an offered was heard at $15.80 per barrel but there were no buyers.
Traders said supplies remained ample and there were no signs that Japan would pick up summer demand this month.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
